title: Word Search II
keyIdea: Insert all words into a trie (store the full word at its end node). DFS from every cell, moving through the grid and the trie together; stop as soon as the trie has no link for the next letter. When a node holds a word, add it and clear it. Mark the path with # and restore on the way back.

approaches.name: Word Search (LC 79) once per word
approaches.idea: For every word, try a DFS from every cell.
approaches.why: Words with a common prefix repeat the same walks; nothing is shared.

approaches.name: Trie + one DFS from every cell
approaches.idea: dfs(r, c, node): follow node->links[board[r][c]] or stop; collect node->word; mark #, try 4 neighbours, restore.
approaches.why: One walk serves every word sharing that prefix, and dead prefixes are cut immediately.

quiz.q: Why use a trie instead of searching each word separately?
options: Words with a common prefix share one walk, and the DFS stops when no word continues
It is the only correct way

quiz.q: Why set node->word = "" after adding it?
options: So the same word isn't added again from another path

quiz.q: Why mark the cell # and then restore it?
options: A cell can be used once in a path, but other paths may use it later

quiz.q: Why store the whole word in the node instead of a flag?
options: So the word can be added to ans directly, without rebuilding it from the path
